message.content:
Below is a quick‑look “long‑weekend” calendar for Canada in 2023.  
It lists the holiday, the date range that becomes a long weekend, and the provinces/regions that observe the holiday.  

| Date Range | Holiday | Provinces / Regions that observe it |
|------------|---------|-------------------------------------|
| **Jan 1–2** | New Year’s Day (observed Mon Jan 2) | All provinces & territories |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, SK, MB) | Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba |
| **Mar 18–20** | St. Patrick’s Day (NL) | Newfoundland & Labrador |
| **Mar 31–Apr 2** | Good Friday | All provinces & territories |
| **Apr 15–17** | St. George’s Day (PEI) | Prince Edward Island |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | All provinces & territories |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day (observed Mon Jul 3) | All provinces & territories |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | All provinces & territories |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | All provinces & territories |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day (observed Mon Nov 13) | All provinces & territories |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | All provinces & territories |

> **Notes**  
> * **Boxing Day** falls on Tuesday Dec 26 in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend.  
> * Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in PEI).  
> * If you need the exact day‑of‑week for each holiday, let me know and I can add that detail.
